endorsements.quote: AI processing must seamlessly integrate with existing clinical workflows, where imaging impacts downstream decisions, such as surgery, interventions, and therapies [ 18 ].
However, to incorporate imaging AI into radiology workflows, an infrastructure that efficiently and effectively interfaces with existing operations and infrastructures is essential.

unlisted_practices: Build AI tools compatible with imaging informatics standards such as DICOM, HL7, and FHIR to ensure interoperability.
Use IHE profiles to guide development of AI applications and definition of integration points and workflows.
Train radiologists in the use of AI-augmented processes.
Design AI-based workflows so they do not interfere with established practice or significantly improve efficiency.
Implement standards such as the IHE standard log of events to objectively measure AI system and algorithm performance and workflow efficiency.
Design user interfaces that let users provide feedback with minimal workflow impact.
Provide configurable end points in AI tools so they integrate into diverse healthcare infrastructures across vendors and protocols.
Perform large-scale AI model validation with rigorous evaluation and standardized reporting.

screen.reason: The paper is a perspective/framework article outlining challenges, standards, workflows, and recommendations for deploying AI in radiology clinical workflows (e.g., using MONAI).
